decks.name: LeetCode #15 - 3Sum
decks.description: Find all unique triplets in an array that sum to zero

cards.question: 3Sum: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0. Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

solutions.name: Two Pointers
solutions.explanation: Sort the array, then for each element, use two pointers to find pairs that sum to the negative of that element. Skip duplicates to avoid duplicate triplets. This approach is optimal with O(n²) time complexity.

solutions.timeDescription: Quadratic time where n is the length of the array. Sorting takes O(n log n), then for each element we use two pointers taking O(n), giving O(n²) overall.
solutions.spaceDescription: O(1) extra space for variables. O(n) if counting the space used by the sorting algorithm. O(m) space for output where m is the number of triplets.
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: For nums=[-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]: Sort to [-4,-1,-1,0,1,2]. i=0(-4): no valid pairs. i=1(-1): find pairs [0,1] and [-1,2] but [0,1] works giving [-1,0,1]. i=2: skip duplicate. i=3(0): all positive, break. Return [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]].

solutions.explanation: Sort the array and use a hash map to count occurrences. For each pair of elements, check if their complement exists in the map. Skip duplicates to avoid duplicate triplets. Uses O(n) space but still O(n²) time.
